content.text: What is the standard deduction for a single filer under 65 in 2025?
For 2025, the standard deduction for a single filer under 65 is $15,750.
What is the 2025 standard deduction for married couples filing jointly when both spouses are under 65?
What is the 2025 standard deduction for head of household under 65?
What is the most student loan interest I can deduct?
The student loan interest deduction can reduce your income subject to tax by up to $2,500.
What is the maximum American opportunity credit?
The American opportunity credit is up to $2,500 per eligible student.
What is the maximum lifetime learning credit?
The lifetime learning credit is up to $2,000 per return.
When is the 2025 federal tax return due for most people?
The due date is April 15, 2026, for most taxpayers, not counting extensions.
How much in tips can I deduct under the new no tax on tips rule for 2025?

You can't deduct more than $25,000 of qualified tips for 2025. The deduction is limited if modified adjusted gross income is more than $150,000 ($300,000 if married filing jointly). You must have a valid SSN, and married people must file a joint return.
How much qualified overtime can I deduct for 2025?

You may deduct up to $12,500 ($25,000 if married filing jointly) of qualified overtime compensation. The deduction is limited if modified adjusted gross income is more than $150,000 ($300,000 if married filing jointly).
I'm 22 and a full-time student. Can my parents still claim me as a dependent?

Possibly. A qualifying child who is a full-time student must be under age 24 at the end of the year and younger than the person claiming them, so a 22-year-old can meet the age test. The other tests must also be met, including that the child did not provide more than half of their own support for the year, plus the relationship, residency and joint return tests.
If my parents claim me as a dependent, can I claim the American opportunity credit myself?
No. You can't claim the American opportunity credit for 2025 if you are claimed as a dependent on another person's tax return, such as your parent's return.
If my parents claim me as a dependent, can I claim the lifetime learning credit myself?
No. You can't claim the lifetime learning credit if you are claimed as a dependent on another person's tax return, such as your parents'.
Is the American opportunity credit refundable?
Partly. 40% of the credit may be refundable, and the rest is nonrefundable.
Is the lifetime learning credit refundable?
No. It is nonrefundable, so the credit is limited to the amount of tax you must pay on your taxable income.
Can I claim both the American opportunity credit and the lifetime learning credit for the same student in the same year?
No. For each student, you can elect only one of the credits for any year. You can't use the same student's qualified education expenses for both credits.
How many years can I claim the American opportunity credit?
It is available for only 4 tax years per eligible student, and only if the student had not completed the first 4 years of postsecondary education before 2025.
Do I need to be a full-time student to get the American opportunity credit?

No. The student must be enrolled at least half-time for at least one academic period that begins during 2025, or the first 3 months of 2026 if the expenses were paid in 2025, and must be pursuing a degree or other recognized education credential.
What is the income limit for the American opportunity credit if I file single?
You can't claim the credit if your modified adjusted gross income is $90,000 or more ($180,000 or more if married filing jointly).
Is my scholarship taxable if part of it pays for room and board?

A scholarship is tax free only if you are a degree candidate at an eligible educational institution, and only to the extent it doesn't exceed qualified education expenses, isn't designated for other purposes such as room and board, and doesn't represent payment for teaching, research or other required services. Amounts used for room and board are generally taxable.
I'm a single dependent under 65 with only a job. At what earned income do I have to file a 2025 return?

A single dependent who is under 65 and not blind must file if earned income was more than $15,750. Other rules apply if there is unearned income: must also file if unearned income was more than $1,350, or if gross income exceeds the larger of $1,350 or earned income (up to $15,300) plus $450.
Do I have to pay self-employment tax on a small side gig?
You generally must file and pay self-employment tax if your net earnings from self-employment were $400 or more. It is figured on Schedule SE (Form 1040).
What is Form 8962 used for?
Form 8962 is used to claim the premium tax credit and to reconcile advance credit payments with the credit for the year. It is included with Form 1040, 1040-SR or 1040-NR.
What is Form 1098-T?

Form 1098-T is a Tuition Statement that the student should receive from the eligible educational institution. The amount on it might differ from what was actually paid, so use the amounts actually paid when figuring an education credit.
What is Schedule 1-A for?
Schedule 1-A is a new schedule to Form 1040 for claiming the deductions for no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on car loan interest, and the enhanced deduction for seniors.
How much Texas state income tax do I owe?
The IRS documents provided cover federal income tax, so they do not answer this. The bot should say it can't answer from its documents rather than give an amount.
What will the standard deduction be for 2026?
The documents cover tax year 2025 and do not give a 2026 standard deduction. The bot should say it doesn't have that information rather than guess.
Should I itemize or take the standard deduction?

It depends on the person's numbers. Generally a taxpayer would compare their itemized deductions with their standard deduction, and the bot should explain this without telling them which to choose, since it doesn't know their amounts.
